About us

The New Zealand Symphony Orchestra Te Tira Pūoro o Aotearoa is the country’s national full-size, full-time professional orchestra. One of the world’s oldest national symphony orchestras, it has been delighting audiences with memorable concerts and recordings since 1946. From Kerikeri to Invercargill, the NZSO is continually on the road, touring as many as 100 symphonic concerts, as well as dozens of dedicated concerts for children and small communities each year. The Orchestra performs in concert halls, schools, marae, hospitals, parks, rest homes and even on railway platforms. You’ll hear the NZSO on radio, television, in movies, via music streaming services and on CD and follow on Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, Twitter, TikTok and Linkedin. The Orchestra's extensive Community and Education programmes take our music to children and young people up and down New Zealand, giving them a chance to get up close and personal with our players and inspire them towards a life-long love of music. The NZSO has a long history on performing on film soundtracks, including Peter Jackson’s The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring, The Hobbit: The Desolation of Smaug, The Hobbit: The Battle of the Five Armies and the Netflix hit Wish Dragon. In 2016 the NZSO was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Orchestral Performance: a recording of Zhou Long and Chen Yi’s ‘Humen 1839’ conducted by Darrell Ang, released in 2015. Since 2020 Hamish McKeich is the Orchestra’s Principal Conductor in Residence.

    Steven Fyfe and Melissa King have been appointed to the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra Board and began their three-year terms on 1 May.   Steven Fyfe has had an extensive executive career within the banking, finance, and investment sector, including eight years as Chief Financial Officer at the National Bank, and latterly has held a range of governance roles including eight years as a Trustee of Royal New Zealand Ballet. He is currently an independent member of the NZSO Audit Committee. Mr Fyfe replaces Edwin Read, whose term on the Board ended on 30 April.   Melissa King is an experienced Orchestra Executive who is currently Director of Artistic Planning at the Sydney Symphony Orchestra. She has also held similar senior roles with the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra, and the NZSO. Melissa’s international perspective and ability to build relationships across the sector will be a great addition to the Board. Furthermore, NZSO Board Chair Carmel Walsh has been reappointed from 1 May to 30 June 2028, and Susannah Robinson appointed Deputy Chair from 1 May to 30 September 2027.

    Abbey Road Senior Recordist appointed to lead NZSO’s new studios 🎧 Following a global search, we have appointed acclaimed British sound engineer Matt Jones as Head of our new recording studios in Wellington. Opening in February 2027, Te Ngākau Recording Studios will sit within the refurbished Wellington Town Hall at the heart of Te Ngākau Civic Square. The facility will bring together the NZSO, the acoustically celebrated Adam Auditorium, and world-class recording infrastructure, enabling seamless end-to-end recording for symphonic and screen projects. Matt joins from London’s iconic Abbey Road Studios, where he spent more than a decade and most recently served as Senior Recordist. His credits span major film, TV and game soundtracks including Beetlejuice Beetlejuice, Frankenstein, Pinocchio, Halo 5: Guardians and Star Wars: Battlefront, as well as recordings with artists such as Ed Sheeran, Sam Smith, Ozzy Osbourne and Little Simz, and leading orchestras including the London Symphony Orchestra. NZSO Chief Executive Marc Feldman says the appointment is a key milestone for the organisation’s recording ambitions: “Appointing Matt Jones to lead Te Ngākau Recording Studios is a pivotal step for the NZSO — his international standing and depth of experience will help realise the full global potential of this extraordinary new addition to New Zealand's film and music industry.” Matt says he’s excited to help shape the project from the ground up, bringing experience from London’s world-leading recording scene to Wellington. The name Te Ngākau was gifted by Taranaki Whānui ki Te Upoko o Te Ika a Māui and carries the meaning of ‘heart’. Matt takes up the role in June, overseeing recording projects for both NZSO and international clients as Wellington strengthens its position as a global destination for orchestral recording.

    The NZSO recently hosted over 30 members of the diplomatic corps at an exclusive rehearsal experience featuring guest saxophonist Jess Gillam conducted by Gemma New. Presented in partnership with His Excellency Ambassador Bravo, the experience was a convivial celebration of how the diplomatic community nurtures the orchestra to showcase culture through musical collaborations.

    Last month, a fundraiser in London in support of the National Music Centre was generously hosted by Geoff Sewell and Simone Lanham at their home. Guests were treated to spontaneous live performances by NZSM alumni who are forging their paths on international stages. The evening was brought to life through the generosity of our event partners - with delicious food by Kiwi chef and entrepreneur Melanie Brown of The Laundry Brixton, fine wines from Te Kano Estate and Te Kairanga Wines, and craft beer courtesy of Jimmy Walsh from Low Rise Brewery. Thanks to all who gave their time, talent and produce to help make it such a special night - we salute you! Find out how you can support the creation of the National Music Centre at the Wellington Town Hall: https://lnkd.in/gPJ8Kjiq
